newsitem.title: USA: U.S. green coffee stocks at seven-year low - GCA.
newsitem.headline: U.S. green coffee stocks at seven-year low - GCA.

text.p: Supplies of green coffee housed in U.S. warehouses fell in August to their lowest level in more than seven years, the Green Coffee Association of New York reported on Monday.

Green coffee stocks declined by 93,000 60-kg bags last month, to 1,816,000 bags, their lowest level since May, 1989, the GCA said. Prior to the August figures, a recent low of 1,878,000 bags was seen in November, 1995.

The port of Laredo, Texas, a key receiving hub for Mexican coffee exports, posted the largest decline. Laredo stocks fell by 104,000 bags, to 275,000, the GCA said. Stocks grew by 93,000 bags, to 704,000, in New Orleans, a leading destination for South American coffee.
Warehouse stocks in New York barely budged, falling 2,000 bags, to 238,000. In Miami, inventories declined by 18,000 bags on the month, to 173,000 bags.
The latest decline was well within market expectations. Traders and analysts had forecast a draw of between 50,000 and 200,000 bags for August, with most anticipating a figure under 100,000 bags.
